title: Sandu: The Three Poisons 3
content:
Madam Yu cut her eyes toward the maids behind her.

Jinzhu and Yinzhu caught the cue instantly. Drawing their steel, they swept through the room with ruthless, clinical precision, running down every last one of the several dozen paralyzed Wen disciples. Within seconds, the hall went dead silent.

Seeing her executioners closing in, Wang Lingjiao made one last desperate, pathetic grab for leverage. "You... you think killing everyone here covers your tracks? You think Young Master Wen doesn't know where I went today?! Once he finds out, do you honestly think he'll let any of you walk away?!"

Yinzhu let out a venomous scoff. "As if the bastard is letting us walk away right now!"

"I'm his woman! His absolute favorite!" Wang Lingjiao screeched, backing up on her elbows. "Lay a single finger on me, and he'll—"

Smack!

Madam Yu’s backhand cracked across her face, cutting the threat off at the root. Her sneer was dripping with pure acid. "He'll what? Cut off my hands? Sever my legs? Torch our ancestral halls to the dirt? Raze Lotus Pier with a ten-thousand-man army? Or maybe erect your little supervisory den right over our bones?"

Jinzhu strode forward, blade pointed down. Terror finally shattered whatever was left of Wang Lingjiao’s nerve; scrambling backward across the flagstones, she shrieked at the top of her lungs: "Somebody! Help me! Wen Zhuliu! Save me!"

Madam Yu’s eyes hardened. Stepping down on the woman’s wrist with brutal weight, she cleared her sword from its scabbard. But right as the killing edge whistled downward, a deafening clang sent her blade rebounding violently into the air.

Wei Wuxian and Jiang Cheng whipped their heads toward the door.

The reinforced wooden double doors had blown clean off their iron hinges, splintering against the walls. Striding through the dust was a towering figure draped in pitch-black robes, his grim face carved from cold stone.

Wen Chao’s terrifying personal enforcer—Wen Zhuliu.

Disarmed by the strike, Madam Yu didn't flinch. Snapping Zidian across her chest in a crackling coil of raw amethyst lightning, her voice dropped like ice. "The Core-Melting Hand?"

Wen Zhuliu’s expression remained deadpan. "The Violet Spider?"

Trapped beneath Madam Yu’s boot, Wang Lingjiao’s face was twisted in sheer agony, tears and snot smearing across her swollen cheeks. "Wen Zhuliu! Wen Zhuliu! Are you blind?! Kill her! Kill her right now! Get this psycho off me!"

Madam Yu sneered down at the man. "Wen Zhuliu? Isn't your real name Zhao Zhuliu? A dog who wasn't even born with a drop of Wen blood, yet you scraped and crawled through the dirt just to take their name. The lot of you scrambling to jump through their hoops—is that surname really worth throwing away your own ancestors? Truly pathetic!"

Wen Zhuliu didn't so much as blink. "I merely serve my master."

Listening to them trade barbs, Wang Lingjiao completely lost her mind. "Wen Zhuliu! Look at me! Stop standing around flapping your mouth and tear her apart! Young Master Wen ordered you to keep me safe—is this what keeping me safe looks like?! Move your ass, or I'll tell him everything and have you skinned alive!"

Madam Yu ground her heel down into the girl's pinned wrist. A sickening crunch echoed through the hall, pulling a bloody wail from Wang Lingjiao’s throat.

Wen Zhuliu’s brow gave a faint, irritated twitch. He had taken orders directly from Wen Ruohan to safeguard Wen Chao, despite despising the young master's spineless, petty nature. But reality had managed to sink even lower: Wen Chao had casually pawned him off as a glorified babysitter for this creature. Wang Lingjiao was loud, manipulative, blindingly stupid, and vicious to a fault—a parasite he would have happily crushed under his boot. Yet his loyalty to the Wen patriarch stayed his hand. Fortunately, she found him just as repulsive, ordering him to trail her from the shadows and keep his distance unless called upon. Out of sight, out of mind.

Yet if he let her bleed out right here, Wen Chao would throw a violent tantrum. And if Wen Chao pressed the issue, Wen Ruohan wouldn't let it slide either.

"Pardon the offense," Wen Zhuliu said softly.

Zidian whipped forward in a blur of blinding thunder. Madam Yu snarled, "Hypocritical bastard!"

Wen Zhuliu threw his bare palm upward—and caught the lightning whip barehanded!

When uncoiled, Zidian was saturated with destructive spiritual currents, dialed to whatever lethal frequency its master willed. Driven by pure, murderous fury and wary of the man's terrifying reputation, Madam Yu had poured everything into that opening strike. Yet he had intercepted the arc of raw lightning with his bare skin as if snatching a stray thread!

In all her years dominating the cultivation world, Zidian had never met an opponent who could casually grab its fury. For a fraction of a second, Madam Yu froze.

Seizing the opening, Wang Lingjiao scrambled on all fours across the flagstones. Fumbling into her robes, she whipped out a brass signal tube, shaking it with manic desperation. A whistling streak of crimson flame shot from the cylinder, blowing through the wooden lattice of the window before detonating high into the dusk sky with an ear-splitting screech. Disheveled, eyes rolling in wild terror, she fished out a second and a third flare, screaming like a lunatic: "Come on... Come on! Get over here! Every last one of you, get in here!"

Ignoring the blinding agony in his back, Wei Wuxian shoved Jiang Cheng forward. "Don't let her fire any more!"

Jiang Cheng let go of him, lunging with a lethal palm strike aimed straight for Wang Lingjiao's skull. But out of the corner of his eye, Wen Zhuliu had already closed the gap on Madam Yu, his palm poised to cave in her chest.

"A-Niang!" Jiang Cheng shrieked, abandoning his quarry and throwing himself into the crosshairs.

Without even bothering to turn his head, Wen Zhuliu backhanded him through the air. "Out of your depth."

The strike caught Jiang Cheng squarely across the shoulder. The sheer impact spun him around, vomiting a mouthful of hot blood across the floor. Outside, the twilight sky was shattered by the screech of Wang Lingjiao’s remaining flares, painting the clouds in violent, brilliant crimson.

Seeing her son struck down, Madam Yu’s roar shook the rafters. Zidian erupted into an apocalyptic storm of blinding white thunder!

The concussive wave blasted Wen Zhuliu off his feet, slamming his massive frame straight into the stone wall. Jinzhu and Yinzhu uncoiled twin lightning-charged whips from their waists, lunging in tandem to tie him down. Having trained side by side under Madam Yu since childhood, their coordinated strikes were lethal enough to hold the line.

Seizing the narrow window, Madam Yu hooked Jiang Cheng by the scruff with one hand and Wei Wuxian with the other, hauling both battered boys through the broken doorway.

Disciples were already swarming the training yard in confusion. Madam Yu roared, "Arm yourselves! Form ranks, now!"

She tore across the courtyards, dragging them toward the docks. Moored along the wooden piers were the light skiffs the Jiang youths always used for picking lotus pods and racing across the water. She tossed both boys roughly into the nearest boat, vaulting over the gunwale behind them, pressing two fingers to Jiang Cheng’s wrist to regulate his battered spiritual core.

Jiang Cheng’s injuries weren't fatal. Wiping the crimson from his chin, he rasped, "A-Niang... what do we do?"

"What do you mean, 'what do we do'?!" she snapped. "Are your eyes useless? They came prepared—this fight was locked in the second they crossed our gates. A swarm of Wen dogs will be descending on this house within minutes! Move!"

Wei Wuxian gasped through the ache in his ribs, "What about Shijie? She left for Meishan two days ago—if she comes back—"

"Shut your damn mouth!" Madam Yu snarled, her glare burning like hot coal. "This whole disaster is on your head!"

Wei Wuxian bit his tongue.

Slipping the silver band of Zidian from her right index finger, Madam Yu grabbed Jiang Cheng’s hand and forced the ring onto his finger.

Jiang Cheng stared at his hand in stunned horror. "...A-Niang? Why are you giving me Zidian?"

"Because it belongs to you now!" she said, her voice hard as iron. "It has already recognized you as its master."

"A-Niang... aren't you coming with us?"

Madam Yu stared down at his face. Without warning, she hauled him into her chest, pressing desperate, hurried kisses into his hair, murmuring against his crown, "My good boy..."

The embrace was bone-crushing—as if she desperately wanted to fold him back into her womb where the outside world could never touch him, where nothing on earth could ever tear them apart. In his entire life, Jiang Cheng had never been held by his mother like this, let alone kissed. Buried against her silk robes, his eyes went wide, frozen in stunned bewilderment.

Still clutching him with one arm, Madam Yu’s other hand shot out, clamping down on Wei Wuxian’s collar with enough force to choke the life out of him.

Her teeth were ground so tightly they threatened to splinter. "...You wretched brat! I hate you! I hate you to my dying breath! Look at the ruin you've brought down on my home!"

Wei Wuxian’s chest heaved, completely stripped of words. This wasn't the usual calculated silence or sullen deference; this time, there was truly nothing left to say.

Jiang Cheng panicked, tearing at her sleeve. "A-Niang, please! Aren't you coming with us?!"

Madam Yu shoved him back into the bottom of the boat, right into Wei Wuxian’s lap.

Vaulting back onto the wooden pier, the skiff rocked violently beneath them. Reality crashed over Jiang Cheng in an icy wave: Jinzhu, Yinzhu, hundreds of disciples, and centuries of ancestral artifacts were trapped inside Lotus Pier with zero time to evacuate. A bloodbath was inevitable. As the mistress of the sect, she couldn't run like a coward—yet terrified of losing her only son, her maternal bias had chosen to smuggle them out first.

Knowing this parting was as good as walking to the executioner's block, raw terror seized Jiang Cheng’s throat. He scrambled to jump onto the dock, but a blinding flash of purple lightning snaked from Zidian, binding both boys to the deck in an unbreakable, crackling leash.

Jiang Cheng shrieked, "A-Niang, what are you doing?!"

"Stop screaming!" she barked. "Once you hit safe ground, it will release you on its own. If you run into enemies on the road, it will defend you. Don't you dare come back! Go straight to Meishan and find your sister!"

Whirling around, she leveled an accusatory finger dead at Wei Wuxian’s face, her voice rising to a ferocious shriek: "Wei Ying! You listen to me! You protect Jiang Cheng with your life! You protect him even if it kills you, do you hear me?!"

Wei Wuxian gasped, "Madam Yu!"

"Do you hear me?!" she roared. "Spare me your excuses—answer me right now!"

Pinned beneath Zidian's binding cords, Wei Wuxian could only nod his head with desperate, absolute conviction.

Jiang Cheng sobbed, "A-Niang, Father isn't home yet! Can't we just hold the line together?!"

Hearing Jiang Fengmian's name, something shattered behind Madam Yu’s eyes, rimming them in sudden scarlet.

Yet in the next breath, her pride slammed the door shut. "Then let him stay gone! Am I supposed to be helpless without him?!"

Drawing her blade, she sheared the mooring line in a single strike, driving her boot hard against the stern. Between the rushing river current, the howling wind, and that violent kick, the skiff shot dozens of paces into the open water. Caught in the downstream drag, it stabilized, drifting rapidly toward the heart of the lake.

"Mother!" Jiang Cheng wailed.

He screamed it over and over until his throat tore raw, but Madam Yu and Lotus Pier grew smaller and smaller on the horizon. Once the skiff cleared the harbor, her purple silhouette turned on her heel, longsword in hand, disappearing behind the heavy front gates.

The two boys thrashed against their bonds, but Zidian only bit deeper into their flesh, rigid as tempered steel.

Jiang Cheng let out a feral, desperate howl, thrashing against the floorboards. "Snap! Why won't you snap?! Break, damn you! Break!"

Battered by dozens of lashings, Wei Wuxian’s entire body burned with white-hot agony. Knowing the struggles were futile and worried about Jiang Cheng’s internal injuries, he gritted his teeth. "Jiang Cheng, calm down! Madam Yu might not lose against the Core-Melting Hand—didn't you see her push him back earlier...?"

"How the hell am I supposed to calm down?!" Jiang Cheng roared in his face. "Even if she kills Wen Zhuliu, that bitch fired the flares! What if the main army descends on our home right now?!"

Wei Wuxian knew it was impossible to stay sane, but one of them had to keep their head. He opened his mouth to talk him down, only for his eyes to catch something on the horizon.

"Uncle Jiang!" he yelled. "It's Uncle Jiang!"

Cutting through the water toward them was a massive passenger vessel.

Standing at the prow, his robes fluttering in the river breeze, was Jiang Fengmian, flanked by a dozen disciples. He was gazing toward the docks of Lotus Pier.

Jiang Cheng screamed at the top of his lungs, "Father! Father!"

Jiang Fengmian caught sight of them, a flicker of surprise crossing his face. At a motion from the disciples, the large ship veered toward their skiff. Clueless to the nightmare unfolding ashore, he called down, "A-Cheng? A-Ying? What kind of game are you two playing now?"

The boys of Lotus Pier were famous for their wild antics—playing dead in the water covered in mud was just another Tuesday for them—so Jiang Fengmian hadn't realized the severity of the situation.

Tears burst from Jiang Cheng’s eyes, half-blinded by sheer relief and terror. "Father! Father, untie us! Hurry!"

Jiang Fengmian reached down toward the skiff. "This is your mother's Zidian. It answers only to its master, I doubt it will yield to—"

The second his fingers brushed the purple lightning, Zidian purred, docile as a kitten. Snapping off the boys, it recoiled in an instant, coiling itself into an amethyst ring around Jiang Fengmian’s finger.

Jiang Fengmian stood entirely frozen.

Zidian was Yu Ziyuan’s signature spiritual weapon, programmed with her will as its absolute priority. While it could recognize secondary masters, there was a strict hierarchy. Madam Yu was its unquestioned primary owner; her standing command was to bind Jiang Cheng until he reached safety, meaning even as a recognized master, Jiang Cheng had been unable to override her will.

Yet somewhere along the years, Jiang Fengmian had been registered as its second-in-command. In his presence, Zidian judged the situation secure, releasing its hold.

Madam Yu had never breathed a single word about granting him mastery over her weapon.

Free at last, the boys scrambled upright. Jiang Fengmian’s brow furrowed. "What happened? Why were you bound in this boat?"

Clinging to his father's sleeve like a lifeline, Jiang Cheng babiled, "The Wens attacked Lotus Pier! A-Niang is fighting them right now—she's trading blows with the Core-Melting Hand! I'm terrified she'll be overwhelmed—they fired signal flares, more of them are coming! Father, we have to go back and help her! Let's go, now!"

Every disciple on the ship paled. Jiang Fengmian's breath hitched. "The Core-Melting Hand?!"

"Yes, Father! We have to—"

Before he could finish, purple lightning flared!

Zidian whipped out, binding both boys flat to the deck of the skiff once more.

Jiang Cheng stared up in utter shock. "...Father?!"

Jiang Fengmian spoke with quiet, terrible finality. "I will return. You two keep going. Do not turn back. Do not look toward Lotus Pier. Once you reach the bank, find your way to Meishan to join your sister and grandmother."

Wei Wuxian yelled, "Uncle Jiang!!!"

Shock gave way to manic panic; Jiang Cheng kicked wildly against the gunwales, rocking the boat until it nearly tipped. "Father, let me go! Let me go!"

"I am going back for San-niangzi."

"Then we go back together!" Jiang Cheng pleaded, tears streaming down his face. "Why can't we go back together?!"

Jiang Fengmian looked down at him. His hand reached out, hovering in midair for an awkward, hesitant beat, before resting gently against his son's crown.

"A-Cheng," he murmured softly. "You must take good care of yourself."

Wei Wuxian choked out, "Uncle Jiang... if anything happens to you two, he will never be whole again!"

Jiang Fengmian shifted his gaze toward him. "A-Ying... look after A-Cheng for me."

He stepped back onto his vessel. The two ships brushed past each other, drifting further and further apart into the dark.

Jiang Cheng’s broken shriek tore through the night sky: "FATHER!!!"

The skiff was swept downriver.

Neither of them knew how many hours bled by before Zidian finally loosened its coil, shrinking back into an unassuming silver ring resting on Jiang Cheng’s finger.

Their voices had long since shredded to bloody husks. The moment the cords vanished, neither uttered a single syllable. Without oars, they dropped to their knees, digging their bare hands into the freezing water to paddle against the current.

Madam Yu had claimed that beating would leave Wei Wuxian bedridden for a month, yet right now, beyond the blinding, raw sting across his back, his limbs moved on pure adrenaline. Fueled by feral, desperate frenzy, they clawed at the water. More than two hours later, their blistered, bleeding hands had managed to drag the boat all the way back to the shores of Lotus Pier.

Midnight had long since settled over the lakes.

The heavy gates of Lotus Pier were barred shut. Torches blazed along the perimeter, casting fractured ribbons of moonlight across the dark water. Dozens of floating lotus lanterns bobbed peacefully near the piers.

Everything looked exactly as it always had.

And that tranquil, undisturbed quiet was the most terrifying thing in the world.

Drifting into the center of the lake, they froze. Their hearts hammered so violently against their ribs that neither dared approach the docks—neither had the courage to step onto the bank and see what lay on the other side of those gates.

Tears welled hot in Jiang Cheng’s eyes, his limbs trembling violently. After an agonizing hush, Wei Wuxian whispered, "...We don't use the front gates."

Jiang Cheng gave a numb, hollow nod.

Steering the skiff around to the blind side of the estate, they slipped beneath the boughs of an ancient weeping willow. Its thick roots were anchored in the mud, its gnarled trunk sprawling out over the water, trailing green leaves into the ripples. In happier days, the boys would scramble up that very trunk to sit among the canopy, dangling their fishing lines into the lake.

Tucking the boat behind the curtain of leaves, they crept ashore beneath the cover of the night. Scaling walls had been Wei Wuxian’s second nature for years. Snagging Jiang Cheng’s sleeve, he murmured, "This way."

Jiang Cheng was in a complete daze, his internal compass shattered, blindly trailing behind him along the masonry. Reaching a familiar stretch of the compound wall, they scrambled up to the eaves. A carved row of decorative stone beast-heads lined the parapet, providing the perfect peephole. In years past, local village kids would climb up here to peek at them practicing their sword forms; now, they were the ones peeking through the gaps like thieves.

Wei Wuxian peered over the edge—and felt his stomach plummet straight into the abyss.

The training grounds of Lotus Pier were choked with ranks of armored men.

Every single one was draped in the sunburst robes of Qishan Wen, the scarlet flame embroidery burning as bright as spilled blood.

And alongside the living stood the dead. A mountain of bodies had been dragged to the northwest corner of the yard, tossed haphazardly into a tangled heap of limbs. Standing before the pile with his back turned to the wall was a lone figure, head bowed, seemingly inspecting the fallen members of the Jiang Clan.

Jiang Cheng’s eyes were wildly scouring the courtyard, hunting for any glimpse of purple silk.

Wei Wuxian’s eyes, however, burned with sudden, scorching moisture.

Among that tangled pile of corpses, he recognized far too many faces.

His throat felt like crushed glass, a phantom iron hammer slamming against his temples as a suffocating chill gripped his marrow. He didn't dare let his mind wander to Jiang Fengmian or Madam Yu. Straining to see if the slender boy draped across the top of the heap was Sixth Shidi, the figure standing by the pile suddenly stiffened, sensing a presence, and turned around.

Wei Wuxian shoved Jiang Cheng’s head down instantly, flattening them against the tiles.

Though they ducked in the nick of time, the moonlight had caught the man's face clearly.

It was a youth roughly their age—tall, slender, with delicate, scholarly features, pale skin, and obsidian-dark eyes. Though draped in the blazing sunburst robes, he possessed none of the oppressive, arrogant swagger of his peers, looking far too gentle and timid for an enforcer.

Judging by the intricate cut of his sunburst robes, he was undoubtedly one of the young masters of the Qishan Wen Clan.
